title: Olivia Rodrigo Rocks Out at Surprise Underplay in Brooklyn’s Warsaw: 5 Best Moments
summary: O Rod and her band tore it up one month ahead of The Unraveled Tour's kickoff.
contentText:
When news broke Thursday (Aug. 6) morning that Olivia Rodrigo was playing Brooklyn’s Warsaw — a ballroom-style punk venue nestled in Greenpoint with a capacity of about 1,100 — that very evening, it took less than 30 minutes for the line to start winding around the block as fans biked, Uber-ed and quite literally ran to get in line for tickets, which had to be purchased IRL at the box office. While the venue has played host to plenty of musical legends (Jack White, L7, Stiff Little Fingers, the Prophets of Rage supergroup) over the years, it’s not often a pop star in the midst of their imperial phase performs a one-off underplay like this. (Sam Smith did play Warsaw last winter, but fans had 24 nights to catch them during their residency.)

The hourlong wait for tickets in the brutal 80-some-degree heat was beyond worth it. Ahead of her Unraveled Tour kickoff in Hartford, Conn., on Sept. 25, Rodrigo and her band ripped through 15 songs in 62 sweaty, breathtaking minutes, delivering three of her four Billboard Hot 100 No. 1s (“Good 4 U,” “Drop Dead” and “drivers license”) and nine of the 13 songs from You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, her latest (and perhaps best so far) album, which topped the Billboard 200 for two weeks.

“Thank you for coming, thank you for waiting in the heat,” Rodrigo told the packed crowd at the top of her set, which opened with a one-two punch of “Drop Dead” and “u + me = <3” and wrapped with a “déjà vu” singalong.

Here are five standout moments from the three-time Grammy winner’s intimate, hard-rocking Warsaw show.
